Thank you for sharing your history. To better understand your condition, have you noticed any specific triggers for your gait and limb ataxia, such as certain foods, medications, or recent infections? 

Additionally, can you describe if your ataxia worsens after eating or if there are any associated symptoms like nausea, vomiting, or double vision?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That "drunken" appearance and unilateral clumsiness are concerning. Have you experienced any recent weight loss, skin rashes, or changes in your bowel habits prior to these neurological symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy.

Given your history of Crohn's disease and one year of natalizumab use, the new onset of asymmetric ataxia is highly suggestive of JC virus reactivation. I am requesting your MRI brain images immediately to confirm the presence of non-enhancing white matter lesions. REQUEST IMAGES
